verdict.summary: A platform-automation environment change at 11:01:52 pointed paymentservice's OTLP traces endpoint at a loopback address on the pod itself, so its telemetry never reached the collector and the service disappeared from metrics and traces while still serving traffic normally.
verdict.reasoning: The alert on paymentservice is backed by no data at all: the error-ratio query returned no samples in either window (tr_14874fd233da) and tempo held no paymentservice spans (tr_aa55d31c89b1) - an absence of telemetry, not a rise in errors. Meanwhile paymentservice's own logs run continuously through and past onset with charge requests received and completed and no error-level lines (tr_cbe9caabde68), and the two other services in the blast radius show error ratios that fell to zero in the incident window rather than rising (tr_b0d43b654af2, tr_121df3ef9ced). Caller-side traces still contain PaymentService/Charge spans at a couple of milliseconds, but recorded only by checkoutservice with no child span contributed by paymentservice itself (tr_bb233e6cdb96) - exactly the shape of a producer whose exporter is shipping nowhere. The change log shows the same OTLP traces endpoint variable set to a loopback address and reverted twice earlier the same day, then set a third time at 11:01:52 and left in place, roughly six minutes before onset (tr_a99b0646ea87). The configuration value is itself wrong - a loopback exporter target where a collector address belongs - and that wrongness is the whole failure; nothing was starved, nothing waited on a slow dependency, and the serving artifact is behaving correctly.
open_questions: Whether the hostname difference between the early and late log lines reflects a container restart applied with the config change or unrelated rescheduling.
Why the blast radius listed checkoutservice and frontend when neither showed elevated errors - likely graph-topology expansion rather than observed symptoms.
Whether any real customer-facing charge failures occurred in the unobserved window, since the only positive evidence of health is logs and caller-side spans.
Whether the recurring automation that sets this variable will reapply it after a manual revert.
